description: Post->turn reactor. Subscribes to channel post-created events (subscribeDomainEvents); for each mentioned member of kind thread, dispatches thread.turn.start on that thread with the post as input. NEVER enqueues on the thread that authored the post. Acceptance: (1) integration test against the real engine: a post mentioning @boss1 enqueues exactly one turn on boss1's thread and zero on the author's; (2) a post with no thread mentions enqueues nothing; (3) when the enqueued turn is cancelled (compaction failure, interrupt, session stop) the cancellation reaches the post: correlate post -> messageId -> the error activity carrying requestId, and surface it on the post (j6o: correlation is by post/mention id, never turnId); a test asserting only that a turn was enqueued is tautological; (4) the toolkit is registered in McpHttpServer's live layer by 0uq before this ships, so the woken agent can reply with comms_post.

title: Table-driven test: assert every command type routes to its expected aggregate
description:
Found by the QA lane during /review-pr on PR #2 (t3_bot-l8i), mutation E; verified at source by boss1.

commandToAggregateRef uses 'command satisfies never' in its default branch. That proves EXHAUSTIVENESS (every command has some branch). It proves NOTHING about CORRECTNESS (that each command sits in the RIGHT branch).

Demonstrated: moving case 'thread.pull-request.sync' from the thread branch into the project branch gives server typecheck exit 0 / zero errors, engine test 29/29 pass, ThreadPullRequestReactor 13/13 pass. Fully GREEN. Cause: ThreadPullRequestSyncCommand (packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:1454-1459) carries BOTH threadId AND projectId, so command.projectId resolves in the project branch and the command is silently stamped aggregateKind 'project'.

Contrast: mutation D moved 'thread.create' (no projectId) into the project branch - tests went RED but typecheck was STILL exit 0. So even where something catches it, it is the suite, not the compiler.

Blast radius if it happens: a thread's events, command receipt, and hasEventAfter scope attach to a project aggregate. Same damage class as the original silent-misroute this PR set out to prevent.

Scope of the fix: a table-driven test over the OrchestrationCommand union asserting each command type maps to its expected aggregateKind/aggregateId. Needs commandToAggregateRef exported (currently module-local at apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/OrchestrationEngine.ts:73) or exercised through dispatch.

Deliberately NOT done in PR #2: it is new work, not a line-edit, and widening a 111-line PR to chase it is scope creep. The 39 hand-maintained case labels make this MORE valuable over time, not less - every added command is another chance to put a case in the wrong group.

title: Channel-watch triggering: wake channel members on any post (post-M1; needs damping beyond never-wake-author)
Post-triggered turn on a busy Claude thread emits no turn.started
description:
ClaudeAdapter.sendTurn (apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:4892) treats a sendTurn during a live non-synthetic turn as a steer: it reuses the existing turnId, emits no turn.started event, and offers the message onto the session promptQueue (line 5018). A channel post that wakes a mid-turn agent is folded into the in-flight turn and has no turn of its own. Codex differs: CodexSessionRuntime.ts:2343 gets a distinct queued turn id back from turn/start but keeps activeTurnId pinned to the running turn. Found during t3_bot-c6z recon (Boss3).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the WRONG fix fails):
1. DO NOT fix this by emitting a synthetic turn.started. Fabricating a turn boundary the provider never produced makes the turn record lie about what the provider did, and the projector settles turns from provider session status — a synthetic start would corrupt duration and settlement. Reject any change that adds one.
2. Per-post identity in the channel view MUST key on the post/mention id, never on turnId. A post steered into a live turn shares that turn's id with other posts by construction.
3. TEST: deliver a post to a thread with a live non-synthetic turn and assert the post remains individually identifiable afterwards. Asserting that a turnId exists is NOT sufficient — it passes with the defect present, because the steered post does have a turnId; it just is not its own.
4. State the Codex behaviour explicitly in whatever the UI consumes, so the two providers do not silently differ in what a 'turn' means to the channel view.

title: Unrouted command path writes no command receipt (and has no counter of its own)
description:
Found by blind verification's adversarial pass on PR #2 (t3_bot-l8i), items 4/5, then refined after a partial disagreement from the verifier that changes how this must be fixed.

WHAT IS TRUE, UNQUALIFIED - the idempotency half:
After PR #2, commandToAggregateRef returns null for an unrouted command and processEnvelope early-returns before Effect.exit, so NO status:rejected receipt is written (observed: receipt_for_unrouted -> Option None). Main DID write one: its catch-all routed the command to thread, the decider then rejected it with OrchestrationCommandInvariantError, and the engine's failure branch wrote the receipt. That receipt short-circuits a replay of the same commandId; without it the command re-processes on every retry. This is a real contract difference.

WHAT IS NOT TRUE, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG - the telemetry half:
Do NOT write this up as 'we lost observability on the unrouted path' and do NOT restore the counter the way main emitted it. Main had no unrouted path at all. What main metered was a successfully-routed THREAD command - aggregateKind 'thread' with an aggregateId of whatever thread the payload happened to name - which the decider then rejected. That is MISATTRIBUTED telemetry, not observability. An operator reading it sees an elevated thread-command failure rate pointing at a specific innocent thread; they never see 'a command was unroutable'.

So the branch lost WRONG data. For a counter anyone alerts on, wrong attribution is plausibly worse than absence: it inflates a real metric and sends the investigation at the wrong aggregate. The regression is in telemetry VOLUME, not telemetry QUALITY.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, written to stop this being closed the wrong way:
1. Restore the rejected-receipt write for the unrouted path, so replay short-circuits as it does for every other rejection.
2. If a counter is added, it must be a signal OF ITS OWN identifying an unrouted command. It must NOT reuse main's shape (aggregateKind 'thread' + a payload-derived aggregateId). A fix that reintroduces the misattribution is a regression dressed as a fix.
3. CLAUDE.md requires stated motivation for instrumenting a statically unreachable branch. The motivation: if a build-time escape ever makes it reachable, an operator has no signal at all.

PRIORITY CONTEXT - why this is a bead and not a blocker on #2:
On main that path is REACHABLE (a threadId-bearing channel command compiles straight into the catch-all and misroutes silently - the exact defect #2 closes). On this branch it cannot compile: TS1360 at OrchestrationEngine.ts and at decider.ts. The gap sits on a path strictly harder to reach than the one it replaced, and the dispatching caller still receives a typed failure, so it is not silent to the client.

SEQUENCE, for anyone reconstructing this later: main (silent misrouting, survivable) -> 75328cd0b (compile-time exhaustiveness, FATAL at runtime - killed the worker fiber) -> d46a978a8 (compile-time exhaustiveness, survivable). The fiber-kill was introduced and closed within this PR; it was never on main.

title: Channel aggregate kind: add 'channel' to OrchestrationAggregateKind, widen aggregateId, make commandToAggregateRef exhaustive (no default)
Agent-originated turn dropped when thread is compacting
description:
ProviderCommandReactor.ts:1521 queues thread.turn-start-requested events into turnsAfterCompaction while a thread compacts, and cancelTurnsAfterCompaction discards them on compaction failure with a human-facing 'Send this message again to continue.' message. A turn triggered by a channel post has no human to resend it, so the post is silently dropped. Found during t3_bot-c6z recon (Boss3).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the WRONG fix fails):
1. A post-triggered turn cancelled by compaction failure MUST become OBSERVABLE — re-enqueued, or the originating post marked failed somewhere its author and the channel view can see. 'It no longer reaches the human-facing message' is NOT sufficient; silence is the defect, not the wording.
2. The fix MUST NOT reuse the existing human-facing instruction for an agent-originated turn. Telling a reader who does not exist to retry is the same bug with better copy.
3. Any retry MUST be bounded and the bound MUST be stated. An unbounded re-enqueue turns a compaction failure into a wake loop, which is the failure mode t3_bot-64d exists to cap.
4. TEST: drive an actual compaction failure with a post-triggered turn queued behind it and assert the turn is re-enqueued OR surfaced as failed. A test that asserts only that cancelTurnsAfterCompaction was called is tautological — it passes with the defect fully present.
5. Distinguish agent-originated from human-originated turns at the point of cancellation, or state why one path serves both.
close_reason: Not a bug: cancelTurnsAfterCompaction appends an error activity keyed by requestId (tested). Requirement moved into 75k criteria.

title: Channel aggregate: channel/membership/post/mention in OrchestrationEngine
Pin node to ^24.13.1 or relax engines; engine-strict is off so mismatch is silent
CI: upstream workflows target blacksmith-* runners the fork lacks; every job queues forever. Port ci.yml Check/Test jobs to ubuntu-latest or disable
rigor toolkit: RIGOR_UI_RE 'tsx?' matches plain .ts so every TS PR fires the Design lane (skills_library, not this repo)
Channel decider+projector+persistence: channel.*/membership/post events, ProjectionChannels repo, migration 051, post bodies in projection table
design:
PROJECTION SHAPE, derived from the ChannelGateway seam boss3 landed (apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/comms/channelGateway.ts). Read the seam before changing any of this - it is the contract, not a suggestion.

Four operations the projection must answer cheaply:

1. getChannelForMember(name, threadId) -> Option<Channel>
   Needs a channel lookup BY NAME plus a membership test for a memberId. So: unique index on channel name, and an index on membership(memberId) - this is the one place memberId is the right key. Note the seam requires a non-member and a non-existent channel to be INDISTINGUISHABLE: an agent must not be able to probe for channels it is not in. Do not return a different error for the two cases.
   Channel carries its full members array, so this read joins membership.

2. getPost(channelId, postId) -> Option<ChannelPostRecord>
   Point lookup scoped BY CHANNEL. A post in another channel returns None, same as missing. Exists so reply can validate a parent without paging history - a lookback bounded by page size silently refuses replies to older posts.

3. readPosts({channelId, limit, cursor}) -> {posts, nextCursor}
   Oldest first, ASCENDING by sequence. Cursor is opaque and points AFTER the last post returned. nextCursor null when no newer posts exist. limit is a maximum, not an exact count (1..200, enforced at the tool schema; the gateway may assume the range).
   So posts need a monotonic per-channel ordering column the cursor encodes. Use the event sequence.

4. createPost(input) -> {postId, createdAt}
   Typed failures: ChannelStoreUnavailable | ChannelWriteConflict | ChannelMembershipRevoked | ChannelMentionUnresolvable.
   The DECIDER is the enforcement point for the last two (pm ruling 184735): reject a post from a non-member, and reject a post carrying a mention that does not resolve to a current member - rejected WHOLE, never silently dropping the mention, because a post that drops a mention wakes nobody while looking sent. The toolkit's pre-check is for the agent-readable error; the aggregate is the guarantee, since the check and the write are not atomic.

POST RECORD FIELDS (ChannelPostRecord): postId, authorHandle, body, mentions (handles), parentPostId, createdAt.
Note authorHANDLE, not authorRef, on the read side - the gateway never exposes memberId to the agent. The event payload carries authorRef AND authorHandle; the projection serves the handle.

BRANDING, flagged by boss3 in the seam header: ids are plain string there as a staged simplification. When the aggregate brands them, ChannelMemberHandle surfaces in handlers.ts (mention resolution) and tools.ts (what the agent sends/receives). The compiler finds every site, but the landing spans more than the aggregate - coordinate with boss3 rather than branding unilaterally.

ROUTING HAZARD, learned in l8i: no channel.* command payload may carry a top-level field named threadId. A thread member's memberId IS a ThreadId, but naming the field threadId routes the command to the THREAD aggregate silently (commandToAggregateRef reads command.threadId). The seam's ChannelMember comment says the same thing. Field is memberId, always.

title: Projector default silently drops unhandled events; make it exhaustive
description:
Found while implementing yyd. Same class as the l8i router catch-all, in the other half of the pipeline.

apps/server/src/orchestration/projector.ts projectEvent ends in:
  default:
    return Effect.succeed(nextBase);

So an event type the projector does not case is SILENTLY DROPPED and the read model is returned unchanged. There is no type error, because the default absorbs every unhandled member of the OrchestrationEvent union.

OBSERVED, not theorised: when channel events were added to the contracts union in yyd, both OrchestrationEngine.commandToAggregateRef and decider.ts failed the build with TS1360 and told me exactly what to handle. The projector did not. It typechecked clean while dropping all seven channel events on the floor, which would have left readModel.channels permanently empty and made every requireChannel fail at runtime against a green build. Caught by reading the file, not by any gate.

WHY IT IS NOT FIXED IN yyd: converting the default to 'command satisfies never' changes how EVERY aggregate's events are handled, forces a decision on every currently-unhandled event type, and is not scoped to the channel work. Doing it inside yyd would be the scope creep that turns a feature PR into a refactor.

FIX DIRECTION: end projectEvent's switch with 'event satisfies never' the way decider.ts:2020 and commandToAggregateRef already do. Expect it to surface a list of event types the projector currently ignores - each needs an explicit case, even if that case is a documented no-op returning nextBase. The value is that the no-ops become deliberate and the next new event type cannot be forgotten.

ACCEPTANCE (observable behaviour, not mechanism): adding a new member to the OrchestrationEvent union without giving projectEvent a case for it FAILS THE BUILD. Verify by adding a throwaway event type to the union and confirming the build breaks at projector.ts, then reverting.

title: Channel events are a replay one-way door: old binaries fail bootstrap on aggregateKind=channel
description:
Found by the Contracts lane during /review-pr on PR #2 (t3_bot-l8i). RESOLVED as a decision by boss1 before starting yyd. Read the CORRECTION below before acting - my original framing offered a fix that does not work.

THE FAILURE, unchanged and real:
A pre-channel binary's OrchestrationAggregateKind is Schema.Literals(['project','thread']) and REJECTS aggregateKind 'channel'. OrchestrationEventStore.readFromSequence decodes rows via Effect.forEach(rows, decodeEvent) - fail-fast, no per-row tolerance, and it does NOT use the repo's own ForwardCompatibleArray (baseSchemas.ts:85). ProjectionPipeline.bootstrapProjector replays from sequence 0 at startup. So ONE undecodable row fails the whole environment bootstrap, not just one read. Same shape as the attachment replay limit documented in docs/internals/providers.md.

CORRECTION - option (a) in my original description was a CATEGORY ERROR. Do not implement it.
I originally offered 'advertise a channels capability on the environment descriptor and negotiate it the way pull-request linking does'. That does NOT fix this. Verified: capabilities are hardcoded in the server's own descriptor (apps/server/src/environment/ServerEnvironment.ts:215-240, e.g. threadPullRequests: true) and are sent to CLIENTS over RPC to tell them what this server supports. Nothing in the replay path consults them. A server advertising channels:false still has to decode whatever is already in its own SQLite at boot, and still dies on the row. The capability pattern solves CLIENT-vs-SERVER skew; this is an OLD-BINARY-READS-NEW-ROWS problem on a different axis entirely. Implementing the flag would look like a fix, pass review, and leave the failure exactly where it was.

THE REAL OPTIONS ARE ONLY TWO:
(1) Make the event-store decode tolerant - skip or quarantine rows whose type/kind this binary does not know, so an unknown aggregate degrades instead of bricking boot. This is the durable fix and it is where ForwardCompatibleArray would belong. It is also a change to the replay path shared by every aggregate, so it is NOT M1 work.
(2) Accept it as a one-way door and write it down.

DECISION FOR M1: option (2). Channel events are a one-way door. Once an environment has written one, it cannot be downgraded to a pre-channel binary without failing to start.
Rationale: M1 runs one binary on one machine (Walt's), so realised downgrade risk is near zero, and AGENTS.md says design for current requirements only. Option (1) is real machinery on a path shared by every aggregate, and buying it now to protect a scenario M1 does not have is exactly the 'introduce machinery because it looks architecturally impressive' that AGENTS.md warns against.
CONDITION THAT REOPENS THIS: the moment channels ship anywhere with independently-upgrading environments - upstream, a relay/tunnel host, or a desktop build users can roll back - option (2) stops being acceptable and option (1) becomes required. That is a real one-way door and it should be a conscious crossing, not a discovery.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- docs/internals states channel events are a one-way door with no supported downgrade, and says why the capability descriptor does not address it (so the category error is not re-derived).
- Do NOT add a 'channels' capability flag believing it solves replay.
- yyd may proceed on this decision.
